name: RC4558IDR
title: RC4558: dual general-purpose op amp, 10 V to 30 V, low noise
summary: A dual bipolar op amp, compensated inside, for ±5 V to ±15 V supplies. Each channel gives 4 MHz gain-bandwidth, 2.2 V/µs slew, 7 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz and 0.0001 % THD+N, drawing 2.5 mA for the pair. RC4558 covers 0 °C to 70 °C and RC4558I –40 °C to 85 °C; RC4558IDR is the RC4558I in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: ±5 V to ±15 V (10 V to 30 V total); ±18 V absolute
0.3 mV typ, 6 mV max at 25 °C; 7.5 mV max full range
7 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz; 6.5 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz
±13.8 V typ into 2 kΩ at ±15 V

circuits.title: Single-ended input to differential output conversion
circuits.description: Both halves of one RC4558 on a single 15 V supply turn a 2 V to 10 V single-ended signal into a ±8 V differential pair. Amplifier 1 follows VIN, giving VOUT+. Amplifier 2 takes VOUT+ into its inverting input through R1 with R2 as feedback, while R3 and R4 halve the 12 V reference onto its noninverting input; with the four resistors equal its output VOUT– is VREF minus VIN. Both outputs then span 2 V to 10 V, VDIFF = 2 × VIN – VREF, and the common-mode level is VREF / 2.

parts.note: amplifier 1 is the follower, amplifier 2 the inverting stage
measured within 2 % of value, as are R2 to R4

notes: VDIFF is taken between VOUT+ and VOUT–.
Resistors of 6 kΩ or less keep their noise below the amplifier's when system noise matters.

circuits.title: Noninverting amplifier
circuits.description: One amplifier as a noninverting stage on split supplies: VIN enters the noninverting input through RIN, RF runs from the output back to the inverting input and RG from the inverting input to ground. Each supply pin has a 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitor to ground; on a single supply VCC– goes to ground and only the VCC+ capacitor stays. Amplifier 2 is unused.

parts.note: low-ESR ceramic, at VCC–; dual supply only

notes: RF and RG sit close to the inverting input to keep its stray capacitance small.

equations.name: Inverting stage output
equations.expr: VOUT– = VREF × R4 / (R3 + R4) × (1 + R2 / R1) – VIN × R2 / R1

where.R4: lower resistor of the reference divider

equations.name: Differential output
equations.expr: VDIFF = VOUT+ – VOUT– = VIN × (1 + R2 / R1) – VREF × R4 / (R3 + R4) × (1 + R2 / R1)

operation.text: Two internally compensated op amps in one package, stable without outside parts. They run from 10 V to 30 V in total (±5 V to ±15 V), with 6.5 nV/√Hz noise at 10 kHz and 0.0001 % THD+N at 1 kHz, and suit audio work such as AV receivers, mixers, soundbars and wireless speakers. Broad input ranges, common-mode and differential, and freedom from latch-up make them suited to voltage followers. The two amplifiers are matched in gain and phase.
Each amplifier is built from bipolar transistors: a differential transistor pair at the inputs and an on-chip compensation capacitor.
Gain-bandwidth product is 4 MHz, common-mode rejection 94 dB, slew rate 2.2 V/µs, all typical. CMRR, in dB, compares the input offset shift with the common-mode input change that causes it.
The part is on whenever its supply is connected. Either amplifier works from a single supply or from split supplies.

RC4558 is rated 0 °C to 70 °C and RC4558I –40 °C to 85 °C. Package letters: D is SOIC-8, DGK VSSOP-8, P PDIP-8, PS SO-8, PW TSSOP-8; R marks tape and reel. RC4558IDR is the RC4558I in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel, marked R4558I.
Specified for ±5 V to ±15 V. Supplies beyond ±18 V can damage the part for good. Put 0.1 µF bypass capacitors near the supply pins against noise or high impedance in the supply.

Fit a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor from each supply pin to ground as close to the part as possible; one capacitor from V+ to ground does on a single supply. Keep a ground plane, with analog and digital grounds apart and their return currents in mind. Route input traces short and away from supply and output traces, crossing a noisy trace at right angles when they must meet. Place external parts near the pins, with the feedback pair RF and RG tight against the inverting pin. Guarding sensitive traces with a ring driven from a low impedance cuts leakage from neighbouring traces at other voltages.

Built for a 15 V supply, 12 V reference, 2 V to 10 V input and ±8 V differential output. Linearity depends on the input common-mode range and output swing, so the outputs are held inside 2 V to 10 V; the transfer curves are swept from 0 V to 12 V, but the circuit is meant for inputs of 2 V to 10 V. With 4 MHz gain-bandwidth, signals must stay under 4 MHz. The VOUT– transfer rests on R1 to R4, so tight-tolerance resistors set the accuracy.
